nodes.label: The manifest is generated
nodes.community_name: AGENTS.md (guidance for agents on the plugin repo)
nodes.rationale: After a tool changed in the core, run npm run build && npm run manifest; manifest.test.ts fails on a stale manifest, and a changed manifest needs --accept-capabilities on the next reload.

nodes.label: Nothing starts outside the gateway
nodes.community_name: AGENTS.md (guidance for agents on the plugin repo)
nodes.rationale: The OpenClaw CLI also loads plugins (plugins inspect, skills list), so work that starts the helper runs only from a service, in registrationMode "full".

nodes.label: Upgrading to a new core release
nodes.norm_label: upgrading to a new core release
nodes.rationale: npm install the core from its git tag, npm approve-scripts it, drop the old pin from allowScripts, build, rebuild the helper.

nodes.label: ADR-0009 (core): hooks in the plugin, nearest MCP equivalent
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009 (core): hooks in the plugin, nearest mcp equivalent
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw-only capabilities stay in the plugin and the MCP server gets the nearest equivalent where one exists.

nodes.label: hooks.allowConversationAccess
nodes.rationale: Required because the instructions and the build check are conversation hooks.

nodes.label: Build check
nodes.rationale: An agent that changed a project and did not build it is asked once more before it answers.

nodes.label: Optional tools via tools.allow
nodes.rationale: An agent gets the tools only when its tools.allow names the plugin (or a tool).

nodes.label: skyrim-modding-tools OpenClaw plugin
nodes.rationale: A native OpenClaw plugin serving the core's Skyrim SE modding tools (record lookup across a load order, mods and patches as text projects, build, deploy, install), doing what an MCP server cannot in OpenClaw.

nodes.label: Core-first principle
nodes.rationale: The tools live in skyrim-modding-tools-core, installed from a GitHub tag; a change to a tool, answer, guide or skill is made in the core, never only here. This repo holds only OpenClaw's glue; what only OpenClaw can do (a hook) stays here.

nodes.label: Care with a real backend
nodes.rationale: The tools write into a mod manager's instance: work on a test instance, change other people's mods only through patches, ask before deploying into a profile someone plays.

nodes.label: Instructions in the system prompt
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw drops the instructions an MCP server announces; the plugin puts them into the system prompt of the agents that mod.

nodes.label: Install OpenClaw step (openclaw@2026.10.4)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw is the host: installed globally so npm install can link it for the SDK's types (scripts/link-openclaw.mjs).

nodes.label: OpenClaw is the host, not a dependency
nodes.norm_label: openclaw is the host, not a dependency
nodes.rationale: .npmrc keeps npm from installing OpenClaw as a peer; the gateway supplies openclaw/plugin-sdk/* at runtime, so it must never be added to dependencies.

nodes.label: Plugin config (envFile, env, agents)
nodes.rationale: envFile points at the MCP server's (or any) .env; its folder is where relative paths start and where projects/ is unless SKYRIM_PROJECTS_DIR says otherwise; env sets single settings over it; agents names the agents that mod.

nodes.label: MCP server's tool rules (profile, budget, gate, one retry, latch)
nodes.norm_label: mcp server's tool rules (profile, budget, gate, one retry, latch)
nodes.rationale: The plugin's tools follow the same call rules as the MCP server so both clients behave alike: sequential, direct-only, prepareArguments = coerceArgs.

nodes.label: A tool fails by throwing (MCP error JSON)
nodes.norm_label: a tool fails by throwing (mcp error json)
nodes.rationale: OpenClaw's contract: a failing tool throws, with the MCP server's {"error", "code"} JSON as message. Nothing OpenClaw would grade goes into details: a non-success status there fails the call.

nodes.label: Tools under their own names, outside Tool Search
nodes.norm_label: tools under their own names, outside tool search
nodes.rationale: editRecord rather than skyrim__editRecord, kept outside Tool Search, so a small local model sees the tools without searching.

nodes.label: Skills come from the core
nodes.rationale: Never edit skills/: it is rebuilt from node_modules/skyrim-modding-tools-core. The manifest names skills/Domain/skills, whose children OpenClaw links into its plugin-skills when the gateway starts.

nodes.label: Skills ship with the plugin (no skills.load.extraDirs)
nodes.norm_label: skills ship with the plugin (no skills.load.extradirs)
